name: LocalizationManager
src_typeComment: Drop this in the first scene, assign a LocaleRegistry, done: every LocalizedText in the project reads from it and updates the moment the language changes.  Lookup order for one key: the CURRENT locale, then the FALLBACK locale, then the missing-key display. The fallback step is what makes a half-translated language usable — the lines the translator has finished appear in their language, the rest stay readable in the fallback rather than going blank.

src_serialized.name: registry
src_serialized.tooltip: Every language the game ships with. Create one via Assets > Create > Toolkit > Localization > Locale Registry, or let the Localization Importer build it for you.

src_serialized.name: defaultLocaleCode
src_serialized.tooltip: Locale code used when there is no saved choice and no system-language match.

src_serialized.name: fallbackLocaleCode
src_serialized.tooltip: Locale code consulted when a key is missing from the current locale. Normally the language the game was written in. Leave empty to disable fallback.

src_serialized.name: matchSystemLanguageOnFirstRun
src_serialized.tooltip: On a first launch (no saved choice), pick the locale whose Target System Language matches the device. Only locales that actually declare one can be matched.

src_serialized.name: rememberSelection
src_serialized.tooltip: Persist the chosen language in PlayerPrefs so it survives a restart. A single string does not justify its own save file, which is why this does not go through SaveSystem.

src_serialized.name: playerPrefsKey
src_serialized.tooltip: PlayerPrefs key used when Remember Selection is on.

src_serialized.name: missingKeyDisplay
src_serialized.tooltip: What to show for a key that exists in neither the current nor the fallback locale.

src_serialized.name: logMissingKeys
src_serialized.tooltip: Log a warning the FIRST time each missing key is asked for. Once per key, not once per frame — a LocalizedText on every label would otherwise flood the console.

src_members.name: CurrentLocaleCode
src_members.comment: These call EnsureInitialized like every other public entry point does. They are the ones most likely to be touched FIRST — a language picker reads AvailableLocaleCodes before anything asks for a string — and an expression-bodied property that skipped the lazy-init would report an empty toolkit for no visible reason.

src_members.sig: public string Get(string key, params object[] args)
src_members.name: Get
src_members.comment: string.Format is wrapped because a translator turning "You have {0} coins" into "You have {0 coins" throws FormatException at runtime, in a language nobody on the team reads. Falling back to the unformatted template keeps the game running and names the offending key in the console.

src_members.name: IsTranslated
src_members.comment: True only if the CURRENT locale has the key — i.e. it is genuinely translated, not merely resolvable through the fallback. That distinction is what a translation-progress readout needs.

src_members.name: Rebuild
src_members.comment: Re-reads every LocaleAsset in the registry. DISCARDS anything added by AddOrOverrideLocale — call it only when the registry itself changed, then re-apply runtime files.

src_members.sig: public void AddOrOverrideLocale(string localeCode, string displayName, IDictionary<string, string> strings)
src_members.name: AddOrOverrideLocale
src_members.comment: Adds a language that has no asset at all, or layers text on top of one that does — this is how LocalizationFileLoader feeds a CSV/JSON read at runtime (a community translation, a hotfix wording change) into the same lookup the shipped assets use. Existing keys are overwritten, untouched keys are left alone, so a patch file only needs the lines it actually changes.
